title: Modus II: from printed letters to German

facsimile.region_note: The crop preserves the Alphabetum, Intentio, Literae significantes, and Exemplum secundi on printed page 251.

passage.label: Clavis parallel reader, cipher-apparatus segment 113
passage.note: The stable passage index identifies the printed Intentio within this containing source segment.

cover.label: Exemplum secundi (cover prose sample)
cover.method: OCR-preserving sample of the Latin Exemplum. After the initial printed marker, alternate words are significant; their initials are read in order. OCR errors remain unresolved, so this sample demonstrates the extraction rule but is not silently forced to agree with the separately printed cipher line.

cipher_stream.label: Literae significantes
cipher_stream.method: Human/vision reading of the printed, period-separated letter line; periods are editorially represented as separators.

extraction.rule: For the cover, take the initial of every alternate significant word after the marker. For the separately printed Literae significantes, read each period-separated letter from left to right and remove separators without reordering.

decode.rule: Invert the printed plaintext-to-cipher Alphabetum and substitute one letter at a time.

intentio.diplomatic: Ich bittedich komm von stund an zu mir es thut sehr noth
intentio.translation: I beg you, come to me at once; it is very urgent.

editorial_note: The substitution is fully reproducible, but the decoded transcription matches only part of the printed Intentio because several tiny Fraktur cipher letters remain uncertain. The edition therefore preserves the computed output and the printed target separately; it does not silently repair the cipher stream.
